text: A `List<String>` is assigned to a raw `List`, an `Integer` is added, and `get(0)` is read as a `String`. Where does it fail?
choices: Nowhere — the value is silently converted to the string "42" on retrieval.
At the `add`, because the list checks each element against its declared type argument.
At the assignment to the raw type, which the compiler rejects outright.
At the read — in the compiler-inserted cast, which is why the exception mentions a cast that appears nowhere in the source.
explanation: At run time the list holds `Object` references and is happy to take an `Integer`. This is heap pollution, and it is why unchecked warnings are worth taking seriously: they mark exactly the places where the compile-time guarantee has a hole. The failure arriving far from its cause is what makes it a genuinely nasty class of bug.
